FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2 YEARS

Garden Things flashcards.

Twelve cards about the things a garden holds: the tree at the gate, the watering can, the wheelbarrow with the big wheel. Everyday garden words, ready to name together.

These cards belong to School Garden · Age 2 on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Name it on the way

    Carry two or three cards on your walk — the tree card, the bench card — and tick them off when you pass the real thing. Garden words live on every street.

  2. 02

    Do what the thing does

    Water like a watering can, dig like a shovel, push an invisible wheelbarrow. Tool names stick when little arms do the job in miniature.

  3. 03

    Spot the letter shapes

    Garden things are big and simple — a fence is lines, a bush is a circle, a tree is a line with a cloud on top. Point them out; drawing comes later for free.

  4. 04

    Grown-up tools, toddler words

    The shovel and rake stay in grown-up hands, and that is the game: your toddler names them, points at them, and does the toddler version with a spoon.

      Flower Flashcard for Toddlers

      The card everyone already knows — and that is exactly why it leads the set. One bright flower, arms open, the word your toddler may already say on every walk.

      What this card shows

      Names the thing your child already points at every single walk.

      Spot it outside

      Play colour spotting from the buggy — red bloom, yellow bloom, white bloom.

      What kids learn from it

      Builds the naming habit that makes every pavement a lesson.

      Print it like this

      Print two — one for the pushchair, one for the wall.

      Grown-up tip

      Cracks in the pavement grow flowers too — look down sometimes.

      Teach it, step by step

      Tree Flashcard for Toddlers

      The biggest thing in the garden, with a woody trunk you can touch and leaves you can count. Trees are year-round teachers — blossoms in spring, shade in summer, leaves to kick in autumn.

      What this card shows

      Shows the biggest living thing on the street, bark and all.

      Spot it outside

      Find the tallest one on your street, then stand under it.

      What kids learn from it

      Teaches big and bigger, plus the feel of real bark.

      Print it like this

      Card stock and thick margins — this is a sturdy one.

      Grown-up tip

      Some old trees wear name plaques — stop and read one.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Tree lesson on the Learning Path.

      Grass Flashcard for Toddlers

      The ground floor of the whole garden. Grass is the first surface toddlers walk, sit and roll on — soft, green and tickly on bare toes.

      What this card shows

      Explains the ground every garden stands on, and every bare foot knows.

      Spot it outside

      Take the wellies off on any safe lawn — thirty seconds of glory.

      What kids learn from it

      Builds texture words — soft, tickly, wet — through the feet.

      Print it like this

      Green ink does the work — any paper will do.

      Grown-up tip

      Bare feet teach this one better than any book.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Grass lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Garden Things for Toddlers | Picture Cards & Activities class on the Learning Path.

      Bush Flashcard for Toddlers

      The round, leafy middle child between flower and tree. Bushes are hideouts for birds, homes for hedgehogs and perfect toddler-size climbing-frame shapes to look at.

      What this card shows

      Shows the leafy in-between, bigger than a flower, smaller than a tree.

      Spot it outside

      Peek round one on the pavement walk and say hello to whoever hides.

      What kids learn from it

      Practises size sorting — flower, bush, tree, one neat ladder.

      Print it like this

      Print it small — bushes are the shy ones of the set.

      Grown-up tip

      Blackbirds nest low — a rustling bush gets right of way.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Bush lesson on the Learning Path.

      Garden Hose Flashcard for Toddlers

      The green snake that drinks the garden! The hose reels out, sprays water and makes every watering day an event — the noisiest thing in the shed.

      What this card shows

      Tames the coiling green hose that grown-ups wrestle every summer.

      Spot it outside

      Spot the reel on a neighbour's wall and follow where the pipe goes.

      What kids learn from it

      Grows tool talk — reel, nozzle, tap and the whoosh itself.

      Print it like this

      Laminate it — this card is on watering duty all summer.

      Grown-up tip

      Hose duty is grown-up work — little crews supervise from the step.

      Teach it, step by step

      Watering Can Flashcard for Toddlers

      The plants' own little teapot. The watering can is the garden tool toddlers can really use — fill it, tip it, watch the plants drink. A first job with real responsibility.

      What this card shows

      Puts the first real garden job in picture form — pouring, gently.

      Spot it outside

      Find the can by the shed and spot where its water actually lands.

      What kids learn from it

      Teaches care-for-living-things through one small, tip-able job.

      Print it like this

      Two copies — the outdoor one will get soggy eventually.

      Grown-up tip

      A small jug does the same job without the weight.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Watering Can lesson on the Learning Path.

      Shovel Flashcard for Toddlers

      The digger of the garden. With a shovel, holes happen, soil moves and every dig becomes a treasure hunt — the tool every toddler wants to try first.

      What this card shows

      Shows the digger every toddler wants to test, handle-first.

      Spot it outside

      Spot the shovel leaning by back doors all down your street.

      What kids learn from it

      Plants tool respect — heavy, pointy and never a toy.

      Print it like this

      Print it alongside the rake — the pair belongs together.

      Grown-up tip

      Spoons dig too — the tool hierarchy can wait a decade.

      Rake Flashcard for Toddlers

      The leaf-gatherer. The rake's long teeth pull leaves into piles — and a pile of leaves is basically a toddler amusement park. Scratch, scratch, gather.

      What this card shows

      Explains the long-toothed broom that turns leaves into one huge pile.

      Spot it outside

      Count the leaf mountains on front lawns — somebody built each one.

      What kids learn from it

      Teaches why gardens get tidied, and who enjoys the pile most.

      Print it like this

      Autumn printing works — keep it with the wellies by the door.

      Grown-up tip

      Rakes stay grown-up — jumping duty starts immediately though.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Rake lesson on the Learning Path.

      Wheelbarrow Flashcard for Toddlers

      One wheel, two handles and a big red tub that carries everything — soil, leaves, tools, sometimes a very happy toddler. The garden's lorry.

      What this card shows

      Names the one-wheeled hauler that moves soil, leaves and occasionally toddlers.

      Spot it outside

      Spot barrows standing in gardens, loaded or empty, all year round.

      Feeds transport talk — load it, push it, tip it out.

      Print it like this

      Fence Flashcard for Toddlers

      The garden's outline. The fence goes all the way around, keeps the ball in and the world out, and is the best counting wall a toddler will ever meet.

      What this card shows

      Explains the line that holds the garden in and the world politely out.

      Spot it outside

      Pick a fence and find the gate, the latch and the gap.

      What kids learn from it

      Sharpens boundary talk — inside, outside, gate, keep it shut.

      Print it like this

      Ordinary paper is fine — fences are the everyday sort of card.

      Grown-up tip

      Fingers out of gaps — the rule says itself once, then often.

      Teach it, step by step

      Garden Bench Flashcard for Toddlers

      The sit-down part of the garden. The bench is where snacks happen, stories get read and tired legs rest — the finishing line of every garden adventure.

      What this card shows

      Names the sit-down spot where garden adventures end and snacks begin.

      Spot it outside

      Walk there together, sit down, and let the whole garden slow to a stop.

      What kids learn from it

      Encourages resting on purpose — a skill grown-ups borrow constantly.

      Print it like this

      It goes last in the stack — the promised rest stop.

      Grown-up tip

      Bench snacks taste better outdoors — take the good ones.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Garden Bench lesson on the Learning Path.
